text:
**For most buyers, LiFePO4 is the better choice.** It lasts several times longer, is less prone to violent failure, and is now the standard in nearly every current model. NMC mainly makes sense if you need the lightest possible unit or already own one that works.

**Why LiFePO4 usually wins**

- **Cycle life:** The sources put LiFePO4 at roughly 3,000 to 6,000 cycles to 80% capacity and NMC at about 500 to 1,000. [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/) and [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/) show Anker's and Jackery's LFP models rated for 3,000 to 4,000 cycles, versus 500 to 800 for their NMC predecessors. Daily use is the case where this matters most. Occasional use, such as a few outages a year, may never reach the NMC limit, and the battery will age from time alone.
- **Safety:** In small-cell lab tests, LFP cells released less heat and gas when they failed, and NMC cells were more likely to ignite. [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/) and [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/) both note that LFP is not fireproof and that a battery management system still matters.
- **Price:** The gap has mostly closed. [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc) reports a median of $0.55 per Wh for LiFePO4 versus $0.95 for NMC, and NMC now mostly appears in compact or legacy units.

**Where NMC still has an edge**

- **Weight:** NMC stores more energy per pound. The advantage is modest in finished stations, roughly 10% to 16% in the medians these guides report, because the inverter, case and fans weigh the same regardless of chemistry. [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/) and [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc) both make this point. It matters most for portable units you carry on hikes.
- **Light use:** A unit used a few weekends a year may outlast its useful life either way.

**Caveats:** The sources disagree on exact numbers. Some quote NMC cycle life as 500, others as 1,000 to 2,000, and the thermal-runaway temperatures they cite come from different test setups. Several are affiliate-supported sites, so check the specs on the model you're considering. Also check each model's charging temperature range, since that varies by brand.
